raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

The ROCm AITER sparse-MLA indexer decode path allocates a fresh fp32 logits tensor on every call to `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`: `(heads, B*next_n, max_model_len)` on the stage1 3D path, or `(B*next_n, max_model_len)` on the gfx942/gfx950 fused 2D path. With long context and a large running batch the per-call working set is multi-GiB; across ~60 layers per decode forward the caching allocator fragments and OOMs. Prefill had the same problem and got `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` plus chunking in #36178. This is the decode mirror.

Two pieces, decode-only, ROCm-only:

- the fp32 logits buffer is now drawn from a per-process workspace keyed by (device, shape) and refilled with `-inf` between calls, so no per-layer alloc/free of multi-GiB tensors;
- `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB` (default 4096) bounds the per-call working set. When a single call would exceed the budget the batch is split into sub-batches that fit and copied into the full output. The aiter kernel does not consume `schedule_metadata` on ROCm, so the metadata doesn't need to be re-derived per chunk. Set to 0 to restore the legacy unbounded behaviour.

Prefill is not touched. The CUDA path is not touched (this file only runs on ROCm via the AITER sparse-MLA backend). Both `_ON_GFX942` and `_ON_GFX950` are covered, plus the stage1 3D else-branch that older arches still hit.

Related: #36178 is the prefill-side mirror (same shape of fix, opposite forward-pass phase). #41002 is in flight in the same area, happy to rebase on top of it after it merges.

## Test Plan

1. Numeric equivalence test added at `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_decode.py`. Skipped on non-ROCm and when the AITER `paged_mqa_logits` module is not importable, so it sits with the rest of the ROCm-only kernel tests. On a ROCm gate it asserts the chunked path returns bit-identical logits to the full-batch call.

   ```bash
   pytest -s -v tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_decode.py
   ```

2. Synthetic micro-bench on a single MI355X (gfx950), 60 back-to-back calls into `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` with a pre-allocated paged kv at `B=1024, next_n=1, heads=64, head_dim=128, block_size=64, max_model_len=131072`. Stress shape, picked so the 3D per-call working set is well above any reasonable budget. Measured peak `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` minus the paged-kv baseline, sweeping `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB` against the legacy code.

3. End-to-end re-run of the GLM-5.1-FP8 customer repro that motivated this:

   ```bash
   vllm bench serve --random-input-len 1 --random-output-len 2 --num-prompts 1024 \
       --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 0 \
       --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 -tp 8 --enforce-eager
   ```

## Test Result

Indexer working set at the high-water mark, 60-layer loop:

| setting                                            | indexer working set @ peak |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------: |
| legacy (no patch)                                  |                  33792 MiB |
| `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB` unset (= 4096) |                  ~4160 MiB |
| `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB=2048`           |                  ~2080 MiB |
| `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB=1024`           |                  ~1040 MiB |

The 33.8 GiB legacy delta is exactly `heads * B * next_n * max_model_len * 4` bytes for the 3D stage1 buffer; chunking brings it down to `chunk_b * heads * next_n * max_model_len * 4` plus a one-shot 2D accumulator. Wall time across all four settings stays between 1.09 and 1.24 s for the 60-call loop, the only overhead is one `copy_` per chunk into the persistent output buffer.

End-to-end on GLM-5.1-FP8, the decode-time HIP OOM that originally fired at ~24 GiB per layer no longer occurs; 1017/1024 prompts succeed, the 7 remaining failures are bench-client side ("never received a valid chunk") and clear with `--max-concurrency 256`.

Thanks for the review. Pushed 0f37431:

- 2D helper: round `rows` up to the next pow2 for the cache key, fill only `[:rows]`, return the contiguous leading-dim slice. Cache size now bounded to O(log2(max_num_seqs * next_n)) entries per (device, cols).
- 3D helper: same pow2 rounding. The workspace stays sized to `alloc_rows` because `ws[:, :rows, :]` is non-contiguous and the AITER `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernel requires contiguous output. The kernel only writes `[:, :rows, :]` (it iterates over `q_fp8`'s batch dim, not the workspace), so the result is sliced after the `sum(dim=0)`. The chunked 3D path slices the same way before the `copy_`.
- Race condition: didn't add a buffer pool. Callers run on the per-rank vLLM v1 forward thread, so a shape-colliding concurrent fill can't happen in normal use. The comment block above the helpers now calls this out and notes that any multi-threaded caller has to allocate its own buffer.
- Added `test_decode_workspace_rounding` covering the helper bookkeeping.

- #41002 moved the indexer buffers onto the workspace manager and reserves the decode logits buffer in the profiling early-exit, so it's accounted for before the KV cache gets sized
- #56214 added `_max_decode_logits_rows`, which caps that reservation at max_num_seqs * (1 + spec tokens) instead of max_num_batched_tokens

If someone hits this on another arch I can redo it scoped to stage1 with the reservation fixed, but as is it adds risk for no gain.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a memory budget and batch chunking mechanism for the ROCm sparse-MLA indexer during the decode phase to mitigate memory fragmentation and potential OOM errors. It implements a persistent workspace to reuse tensors across layers and adds a sanity check test. The review feedback identifies a critical issue where caching tensors for every unique batch size could lead to excessive memory consumption in dynamic serving environments. Suggestions were provided to round up the cached dimensions to powers of two and to address potential race conditions when accessing the shared workspace.

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The workspace dictionaries `_decode_ws_3d` and `_decode_ws_2d` use the exact `rows` (which is `batch_size * next_n`) as part of the key. In a dynamic serving environment, the decode batch size changes frequently as requests are added or completed. This will lead to the allocation and caching of many large tensors (e.g., for every observed batch size), which can quickly consume all available GPU memory and cause an OOM. For example, with `max_model_len=131072` and `heads=64`, caching every batch size from 1 to 256 would consume an enormous amount of memory.

nodes.body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

To prevent memory bloat from caching every possible batch size, consider rounding up the `rows` dimension to a power of two or a fixed multiple (e.g., 32). This limits the number of unique shapes stored in the dictionary. Also, ensure that the `fill_` operation is performed on the requested slice. 

Additionally, note that the `_decode_ws_lock` only protects the dictionary and the `fill_` call. If multiple threads call this function concurrently for the same shape, they will share the same tensor, leading to a race condition where one thread's `fill_` can corrupt another thread's computation. If concurrency is possible, a pool of buffers should be used instead.

```suggestion
def _decode_workspace_3d(
    device: torch.device, heads: int, rows: int, cols: int
) -> torch.Tensor:
    # Round up rows to a power of 2 to limit cache entries and prevent memory bloat.
    alloc_rows = 1 << (rows - 1).bit_length() if rows > 0 else 0
    key = (device, heads, alloc_rows, cols)
    with _decode_ws_lock:
        ws = _decode_ws_3d.get(key)
        if ws is None:
            ws = torch.empty(
                (heads, alloc_rows, cols),
                device=device,
                dtype=torch.float32,
            )
            _decode_ws_3d[key] = ws
        
        # Slice and fill only the requested portion.
        res = ws[:, :rows, :]
        res.fill_(float("-inf"))
        return res
```

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Sanity check for the ROCm sparse-MLA indexer decode logits MB budget.
+
+When VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_DECODE_MAX_MB forces a per-call split, the chunked
+path must produce bit-identical logits to a single full-batch call. The
+underlying aiter kernel is deterministic on a fixed shape, so a tiny budget
+that triggers chunking is enough to catch any indexing slip.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_rocm(), reason="Only used by ROCm"
+)
+
+
+def _aiter_decode_available() -> bool:
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.rocm_aiter_mla_sparse import (
+        paged_mqa_logits_module,
+    )
+
+    return rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled() and paged_mqa_logits_module() is not None
+
+
+def _build_decode_inputs(
+    batch_size: int,
+    next_n: int,
+    heads: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+    block_size: int,
+    max_model_len: int,
+    seed: int,
+) -> dict:
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    fp8_dtype = current_platform.fp8_dtype()
+
+    q = torch.randn(
+        (batch_size, next_n, heads, head_dim),
+        device=device,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+    ).to(fp8_dtype)
+
+    num_blocks_per_batch = max_model_len // block_size
+    num_blocks = batch_size * num_blocks_per_batch + 4
+    kv_cache = torch.randint(
+        0,
+        255,
+        (num_blocks, block_size, 1, head_dim + 4),
+        device=device,
+        dtype=torch.uint8,
+    )
+    weights = torch.randn(
+        (batch_size * next_n, heads), device=device, dtype=torch.float32
+    )
+    context_lens = torch.full(
+        (batch_size,),
+        max_model_len // 2,
+        device=device,
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+    )
+    block_tables = torch.zeros(
+        (batch_size, num_blocks_per_batch),
+        device=device,
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+    )
+    block_start = 0
+    for i in range(batch_size):
+        block_tables[i].copy_(

![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

The workspace dictionaries `_decode_ws_3d` and `_decode_ws_2d` use the exact `rows` (which is `batch_size * next_n`) as part of the key. In a dynamic serving environment, the decode batch size changes frequently as requests are added or completed. This will lead to the allocation and caching of many large tensors (e.g., for every observed batch size), which can quickly consume all available GPU memory and cause an OOM. For example, with `max_model_len=131072` and `heads=64`, caching every batch size from 1 to 256 would consume an enormous amount of memory.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

To prevent memory bloat from caching every possible batch size, consider rounding up the `rows` dimension to a power of two or a fixed multiple (e.g., 32). This limits the number of unique shapes stored in the dictionary. Also, ensure that the `fill_` operation is performed on the requested slice. 

Additionally, note that the `_decode_ws_lock` only protects the dictionary and the `fill_` call. If multiple threads call this function concurrently for the same shape, they will share the same tensor, leading to a race condition where one thread's `fill_` can corrupt another thread's computation. If concurrency is possible, a pool of buffers should be used instead.

```suggestion
def _decode_workspace_3d(
    device: torch.device, heads: int, rows: int, cols: int
) -> torch.Tensor:
    # Round up rows to a power of 2 to limit cache entries and prevent memory bloat.
    alloc_rows = 1 << (rows - 1).bit_length() if rows > 0 else 0
    key = (device, heads, alloc_rows, cols)
    with _decode_ws_lock:
        ws = _decode_ws_3d.get(key)
        if ws is None:
            ws = torch.empty(
                (heads, alloc_rows, cols),
                device=device,
                dtype=torch.float32,
            )
            _decode_ws_3d[key] = ws
        
        # Slice and fill only the requested portion.
        res = ws[:, :rows, :]
        res.fill_(float("-inf"))
        return res
```

- 2D helper: round `rows` up to the next pow2 for the cache key, fill only `[:rows]`, return the contiguous leading-dim slice. Cache size now bounded to O(log2(max_num_seqs * next_n)) entries per (device, cols).

The workspace stays sized to `alloc_rows` because `ws[:, :rows, :]` is non-contiguous and the AITER `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernel requires contiguous output. The kernel only writes `[:, :rows, :]` (it iterates over `q_fp8`'s batch dim, not the workspace), so the result is sliced after the `sum(dim=0)`. The chunked 3D path slices the same way before the `copy_`.
- Race condition: didn't add a buffer pool. Callers run on the per-rank vLLM v1 forward thread, so a shape-colliding concurrent fill can't happen in normal use. The comment block above the helpers now calls this out and notes that any multi-threaded caller has to allocate its own buffer.

The OOM I was fixing was the stage1 path on MI355X: back in May the fused paged MQA logits kernel was only used on gfx942, so gfx950 fell into the `[heads, rows, max_model_len]` buffer plus `.sum`, and at long context that one call asked for 24.56 GiB. Since then:
- #42062 enabled the fused 2D `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` path on gfx950 too (`_ON_GFX942 or _ON_GFX950`), so MI355X decode now only needs `[rows, max_model_len]`
- #41002 moved the indexer buffers onto the workspace manager and reserves the decode logits buffer in the profiling early-exit, so it's accounted for before the KV cache gets sized
- #56214 added `_max_decode_logits_rows`, which caps that reservation at max_num_seqs * (1 + spec tokens) instead of max_num_batched_tokens

I also rebased this on main and it doesnt fit anymore. The workspace is locked after profiling and any growth past the reservation raises AssertionError. My chunked fused branch asks for the full output plus a chunk buffer at the same time, which is more than what profiling reserved, so on gfx950 it could turn a config that works today into an assert, and it cant lower peak there anyway since the full output is still allocated. On the stage1 path (non gfx942/950) profiling still reserves heads * rows * max_model_len, so chunking only saves memory if that reservation gets capped too. If someone hits this on another arch I can redo it scoped to stage1 with the reservation fixed, but as is it adds risk for no gain.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a memory budget and batch chunking mechanism for the ROCm sparse-MLA indexer during the decode phase to mitigate memory fragmentation and potential OOM errors. It implements a persistent workspace to reuse tensors across layers and adds a sanity check test. The review feedback identifies a critical issue where caching tensors for every unique batch size could lead to excessive memory consumption in dynamic serving environments. Suggestions were provided to round up the cached dimensions to powers of two and to address potential race conditions when accessing the shared workspace.
